newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SRI LANKA ASKS BUYERS TO RE-TENDER FOR FUEL OIL.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA ASKS BUYERS TO RE-TENDER FOR FUEL OIL.

text.p: Sri Lanka state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) has asked three buyers for its tender to sell 19,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil to resubmit their prices for different lifting dates, a CPC official said on Thursday.
"There is a small problem with the laycan," the official said. "So we called for the three best bidders to improve their prices."
CPC changed the lifting dates to August 30-September 1 from the original August 27-28.

Ealier on Thursday, the official said Japanese trading house, Marubeni Corp made the best bid into the tender at $10.88 per tonne below Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) Colombo basis but for a later September lifting date.
"Marubeni even improved his bid by $1.00 but we want to be fair to them and want the best possible price," he said.
Dutch trader Vitol and major British Petroleum have also been asked to submit fresh bids by 1100 am Sri Lanka time (0900 GMT) on Friday .
Vitol made the next best bid at $11.70 per tonne below Singapore spot quotes fob while BP's bid was at a $13.95 discount, the official said.
The original tender closed on August 13 and was valid for two days.
In its last tender, CPC sold 20,000 tonnes of 3.5 percent sulphur fuel oil at a discount of $14.75 per tonne to Singapore spot quotes on fob Colombo basis, for July 22-23 lifting.
